title: The Day of the Rogue Umbrella
skyStory: The crescent has fattened to seventeen percent and is still hanging around Sagittarius, packing a backpack with snacks it will never eat. Rain rolls in sideways off the water. Mars is excited, because sideways rain is basically weather with a sword. Saturn has put on galoshes and is pretending it chose this. Somewhere a wind chime is playing jazz.

reading: The Tiger wakes up with a spark already lit, and by 9 am you will have two brilliant ideas and a third that is mostly a pun. Keep the pun. It is the only one with legs.

An umbrella will betray you today, either flipping inside out or hiding in the wrong car. This is not bad luck. It is the [[Six of Pentacles]] engineering a chance for someone to share theirs, and you must say yes without immediately offering to carry their bag in return. Huddle. Accept the shelter. Fire that is protected from the rain burns longer, and frankly the Tiger looks great slightly damp.
joel.mission: Tell one person a genuinely good idea of yours and then stop talking for five full seconds to see what they add.
joel.omen: A red umbrella blowing past with nobody holding it. Your idea is ready to travel without you steering.
joel.elementWhy: a spark that refuses to get soggy

reading: Your intuition is running a few minutes ahead of the clock today. At some point you will think of a person and, within the hour, hear from them. Do not act surprised. Act like you scheduled it.

Rainy Sagittarius moons make everyone want adventure but nobody want to leave the house. You are the exception: you can have an adventure from the couch, because you are the one who tells it. Pick a tiny memory, a ferry ride or a strange café or a dog with a hat, and polish it into a story with a twist ending. The ruby on your pinky will catch the lamplight every time you gesture. Gesture a lot.
nancy.mission: Write a one-line weather report for your own mood and post it on the fridge like an official bulletin.
nancy.omen: Two raindrops racing down a window. Bet on the left one. If it wins, an easy yes is coming.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire keeps the rain off

together.text: Trade one idea each that you have been too shy to say out loud. No critique allowed, only the phrase 'and what if' to build on it. Three rounds maximum, or the idea gets too big for the cabin door.

game.intro: A rogue umbrella is loose on the street and Mars is cheering it on. Pick your chase, then guess the other's.
game.question: A gust steals your umbrella. What do you chase down the street first?
